assessments.reasoning: The YCS 257 authors explicitly identify ISETL as the language to which they added a bag type and coordination operations. Their account establishes the direction of the extension relationship.

challenge.method: Could the compound name alone have suggested the wrong parent language?
challenge.results: The authors identify ISETL as the base independently of the compound name. They give the York Linda variant a different role, supplying the design of the operations.

limitations: The added primitives come from a York Linda variant; this does not make ISETL-LINDA an alias for that coordination model.
The relationship concerns ISETL as described by YCS 257. The exact base ISETL implementation and version are outside the abstract's scope.
